stem: A histogram has the following class intervals and frequencies: [10-20]: 8, [20-30]: 14, [30-40]: 20, [40-50]: 12, [50-60]: 6. The class intervals have equal width. What is the height of the tallest bar as a fraction of the total frequency?

per_option_rationale.rationale: Total frequency = 8 + 14 + 20 + 12 + 6 = 60. Tallest bar has frequency 20. Fraction = 20/60 = 1/3.
2/5 = 24/60; this would imply the modal frequency is 24, not 20.
1/4 = 15/60; the student may have mistaken 15 for the maximum frequency.
2/9 = 20/90; the total was mis-summed as 90 instead of 60.

explanation: Total frequency = 8 + 14 + 20 + 12 + 6 = 60. The tallest bar corresponds to [30-40] with frequency 20. Relative height = 20/60 = 1/3.

explanation_sections.punchline: Tallest bar = class [30-40] with frequency 20 out of total 60, giving fraction 1/3.
explanation_sections.approach: Identify the model: equal-width histogram - height = frequency. Sum all frequencies to get N=60. Identify the maximum frequency (20). Divide: 20/60 = 1/3.
explanation_sections.lesson: Always compute the total before forming a relative frequency ratio; a wrong total is the most common trap.
